title: Runtime decision scoring: workings, logs, and regional controls
content:
Purpose:
This note collects the current thinking and open decisions for the policy evaluation component that lives in the control plane and the small runtime adapter in the data plane. Focus: constraints evaluation, scoring math, explainability/logging format, and multi-region overrides.

High-level flow (runtime):
- Request enters data plane router (region-aware).
- Router attaches request metadata (region, customer-tier, route-id, model-variant).
- If request requires policy checks, runtime calls policy-eval-adapter (lightweight, local cache of rules).
- Adapter returns: allow|deny|score + provenance tokens (rule-ids, score_components).
- Router makes routing decision (serve, fallback-model, throttle) based on score + SLO hints.

Design goals / constraints:
- Extremely low p99 added latency per request (< 1.5ms ideally) for common constraints (headers, route tags, quotas).
- Deterministic scoring for auditability (given same inputs + rule-set version -> same score).
- Explainability logs must be compact but reconstructable (no sensitive PII stored).
- Support regional policy divergence: e.g., EU region might disallow a model or require extra checks.
- Backward-compatible rule changes: rules are versioned, and decisions include rule_version id.

Constraint evaluation model:
- Two-phase constraints: static and dynamic.
  - Static: route-level allowlists/blocklists, model compatibility matrix, license tier checks. Evaluated cheaply from config.
  - Dynamic: content-based signals, throttles, recent anomaly heuristics. May require async enrichment (signals from observability).
- Constraints return binary pass/fail plus a small reason code (e.g., STATIC_TIER_MISMATCH, DYNAMIC_RATE_LIMIT, CONTENT_POLICY_FLAG).

Scoring semantics (how we compute decision score):
- Score is a normalized 0.0-1.0 float where higher means more likely to allow full-fidelity serving.
- Score composition model:
  score = clamp(sum_i w_i * f_i(inputs)), 0, 1
  where f_i are normalized sub-scores from 0..1 and w_i are weights (sum_w <= 1) with a residual safety factor.
- Primary components we use today:
  - compliance_weight * compliance_score (0/1 for simple constraints; fractional for ML classifiers)
  - latency_weight * latency_risk_score (based on queue/backpressure predictions)
  - cost_weight * cost_sensitivity (customer-config driven)
  - quality_weight * model_quality_risk (from eval regressions)
- Default weights: compliance 0.6, latency 0.15, cost 0.1, quality 0.15. These are tunable via rollout.
- Notes: keep scoring linear for explainability. Don't bake complex nonlinear transforms in the main control path. Use post-hoc models in offline analysis only.

Explainability logging format (runtime-slim):
- Log lines are newline-delimited JSON (ndjson). Each line is designed to fit in a single logging event (<= 1KB) for common cases.
- Field set (all keys short to save bytes):
  - ts: ISO timestamp
  - req_id: request UUID
  - region: region code (e.g., eu-west-1)
  - route: route-id
  - customer_id: hashed_customer_id (salted HMAC, no raw id)
  - rule_set_v: semantic version string
  - decision: allow|deny|degrade
  - score: 0.0..1.0 (stringified float)
  - comps: list of "k:val" short strings describing component contributions, e.g. ["cpl:1:0.6", "lat:0.2:0.03"] where format is <shortKey>:<componentScore>:<weightedContribution>
  - flags: short list of rule ids triggered (max 6)
  - mask: boolean (true if payload was masked for PII)
  - policy_refs: small list of policy aliases (used for audit linking)
- Example: {"ts":"2025-09-30T12:13:14Z","req_id":"r-12a3","region":"eu","route":"chat-v1","customer_id":"h:abc123","rule_set_v":"2025.09.18","decision":"degrade","score":"0.28","comps": ["cpl:0.0:0.0", "lat:0.8:0.12", "qlt:0.2:0.03"],"flags": ["R-77"],"mask":"true","policy_refs": ["p-chat-safety"]}

Storage/retention and privacy:
- Explainability logs stored separately from full request payloads and rotated: default 30 days, enterprise vary 180/365 days.
- customer_id stored as HMAC to prevent re-identification in logs; original mapping only available in secure vault and via audited export.
- PII masking is applied pre-log using local runtime scrubbing rules (regex + model-based entity detection) controlled by policy metadata. If masking occurs, mask=true is logged.

Runtime caching strategy (to hit latency targets):
- Cache key = sha256(route, model_variant, customer_tier, normalized_request_signature, rule_set_v)
- Normalized_request_signature is a fingerprint of the top-k inputs used for policy checks: headers, route params, first 256 bytes of input text (where allowed).
- TTL: 2s default for high-churn routes, 30s for stable routes with prefix caching.
- Invalidation on rule_set_v change: we embed rule_set_v in cache key so new rules take effect immediately (no global invalidation required).

Multi-region policy governance:
- Master rule repository lives in control plane (global). Each region can have an overlay file containing regional overrides. Overlay applies after global rules; override entries are explicit (cannot silently remove global allow entries, only tighten or add).
- Deployment model: control plane publishes rule_set_v tags per region. Data plane nodes pull rule bundles and validate signatures.
- Edge case: when a regional rule disallows a model used by a customer who is multiregional, runtime will: first obey region rule (deny/degrade), then trigger an async re-route attempt to fallback-compatible variant in allowed region if customer config allows cross-region routing (requires opt-in).

Control plane vs data plane responsibilities:
- Control plane: rule authoring UI, bundle signing, versioning, policy audits, global rollout orchestration, eval pipelines for ML-based policies.
- Data plane: fast local evaluation, caching, masking, telemetry emission, direct enforcement per request.

Decision provenance and audits:
- Each decision line includes a compact provenance token (signed blob pointer) that can be used to fetch full evaluation trace from the control plane audit store for up to retention window. This lets auditors reconstruct full evaluation including ML model inputs/outputs without storing everything on the edge.
- Provenance token format: base64(signed pointer) where pointer = {bundle_id, eval_id, timestamp, shard_id}. Tokens are short (<= 256 bytes).

Operational concerns / emergency modes:
- Fast-fail safe mode: if policy-eval-adapter is unreachable, runtime options: (configurable per-customer) default_allow_with_quota, default_deny, or degrade_to_small_model. Default for PLG is degrade_to_small_model.
- Rollback: rule set rollout supports canary percent, gradual ramp, and automatic rollback if error rates spike or policy eval latency exceeds threshold.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to represent composite rules in explainability logs succinctly? (Tradeoff: full tree vs flat triggered rule ids).
- Should we include a hashed version of the rule text in logs for faster delta detection in offline analysis? Risk: rule text leak.
- Quantization of component weights for smaller log footprint (store int16 instead of float).
- Define exact HMAC salt rotation policy for customer_id hashing across regions.
- Standardize sampling: we should sample 1% of allow decisions and 100% of deny/degrade for full trace retention; but sampling rates should be customer-configurable.

Immediate action items:
- A: Prototype ndjson emitter in runtime adapter and measure added p50/p95 latency. (Assignee: Priya) (GH: pr/428)
- B: Add rule_set_v to all cache keys and validate end-to-end. (Assignee: Alex)
- C: Draft audit-store pointer format and sign/verify toolkit for control plane. (Assignee: Marta)
- D: Ops playbook for safe-mode options and how to flip in incident. (Assignee: SRE oncall)

Notes from offline discussion (Sept 25):
- Prefer linear, composable scores for human interpretability. Keep ML transforms out of the fast path.
- Make explainability logs usable for customer audits: provide a customer-facing redact view and an internal view with provenance pointer.

Appendix: small examples and sketches
- Example cache key pseudocode:
  key = sha256(f"{route}|{model_variant}|{customer_tier}|{fingerprint}|{rule_set_v}")

- Example simple scoring breakdown:
  components = {cpl:1.0, lat:0.2, cost:0.1, qlt:0.0}
  weights = {cpl:0.6, lat:0.15, cost:0.1, qlt:0.15}
  weighted = {cpl:0.6, lat:0.03, cost:0.01, qlt:0.0} -> sum=0.64 -> score=0.64

- Example log with masked payload marker:
  {"ts":"2025-09-30T12:13:14Z","req_id":"r-12a3","region":"us","route":"embed-v2","customer_id":"h:abc123","rule_set_v":"2025.09.18","decision":"allow","score":"0.95","comps": ["cpl:1.0:0.6","lat:0.1:0.015","cost:0.05:0.005"],"flags": [],"mask":"false"}

If you have comments or want me to reformat the log schema to be even more compact (shorter keys, numeric-only comps) I can prototype both and measure bytes/cost.

-- Jordan
